title_en: Jobs (13/20): An Electrician Fixes the Wiring
note_en: 被 marks the passive: 有一根电线被老鼠咬断了 "a wire had been chewed through by a rat." The doer comes right after 被, before the verb, where English puts it at the end with "by"; and the verb rarely stands alone but carries a result, as in 咬断 "bite + snapped" or 刮破 "scrape + broken" (电线被钉子刮破了绝缘层). Chinese uses 被 mostly for unwelcome events like damage, so it is far less common than the English passive.
